content: Tympanic membrane retractions are a condition frequently addressed by ENT surgeons. However, there is currently no established consensus regarding the indications for surgery, the optimal timing of intervention, or the most effective surgical techniques for managing this condition. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of various surgical approaches in the treatment of tympanic membrane retractions. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Ear, Nose and Throat Disorders Group Trials Register, CENTRAL, PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, BIOSIS Previews, ISI Web of Science, CAB Abstracts, LILACS, KoreaMed, IndMed, PakMediNet, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, ISCTRN, UKCRN, ICTRP, and Google. The search was completed on March 17, 2010. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that investigated surgical management of tympanic membrane retraction pockets in either adults or children. Studies were required to use a recognized staging system for retraction pockets. Research involving cholesteatoma or tympanic membrane perforations was excluded from the analysis. To minimize selection and reporting bias, two independent authors collected and analyzed the data. Ultimately, two RCTs involving a total of 71 participants met the inclusion criteria. The first study compared cartilage graft tympanoplasty with a watch and wait approach. It found no statistically significant difference between the two strategies in terms of disease progression or hearing outcomes. The second study evaluated the addition of ventilation tubes to cartilage tympanoplasty and found no additional benefit in terms of hearing outcomes when compared to cartilage tympanoplasty alone. The authors concluded that there is currently no evidence to either support or refute the role of surgery in the management of tympanic membrane retractions. They emphasized the need for higher-quality studies to better determine the effectiveness of surgical interventions for this condition.
